record.paper_title: Unsolved Problems in Visibility Graphs of Points, Segments and Polygons
record.original_question: Characterize exactly which graphs are bar k-visibility graphs, where vertices are horizontal bars and two bars are adjacent exactly when some vertical segment between them intersects at most k other bars.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 19 Characterize bar k-visibility graphs.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let k be a non-negative integer. A bar k-visibility representation of a graph G consists of an assignment of pairwise disjoint, non-degenerate horizontal closed line segments (called bars) in the plane to the vertices of G, such that two vertices u and v are adjacent in G if and only if there exists a vertical (closed) line segment whose endpoints lie on the bars assigned to u and v, and which intersects the interiors of at most k other bars (bars not assigned to u or v). A graph is called a bar k-visibility graph if it admits such a representation. (When k = 0, this recovers the classical bar visibility graphs, which are known to be characterized as a subclass of planar graphs.)

Problem: Give a complete combinatorial characterization of the class of bar k-visibility graphs. That is, determine necessary and sufficient conditions on a graph G for G to admit a bar k-visibility representation.
artifact.status_search_result: The literature on bar k-visibility graphs (Dean et al., and follow-up work on parameters such as edge count, chromatic number, and thickness) addresses bounds and special cases but does not provide a complete combinatorial characterization. The full characterization problem is still cited as open.

status_evidence.title: Bar k-Visibility Graphs (Dean et al.)
status_evidence.snippet: Introduces bar k-visibility graphs and studies edge bounds, chromatic number, thickness; does not give a full characterization.
status_evidence.claim: The defining paper studies parameters but leaves the characterization open.

status_evidence.title: Further Results on Bar k-Visibility Graphs, SIAM J. Discrete Math.
status_evidence.snippet: Further parameter bounds (chromatic number, thickness) for bar k-visibility graphs.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent work refines bounds but does not characterize the class.

status_evidence.title: Parameters of Bar k-Visibility Graphs, JGAA
status_evidence.snippet: Studies graph parameters of bar k-visibility graphs without characterizing them.
status_evidence.claim: No characterization is given; only parameter results.
